exercise.name: Cable Low Seated Row

reference.title: Cable Low Seated Row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder extension, scapular retraction, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row the handle to the stomach, breathe in as the arms reach forward.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s pull, short squeeze, about 2 s return

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can row to the stomach without rocking the trunk back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; add a 1 s squeeze

cues.text: Sit tall facing the low pulley, feet braced on the foot plate with the knees slightly bent; hold the V-handle with the palms facing each other, arms long, chest leaning a little forward.
Breathe out; sit tall, draw the shoulder blades back and row the handle to the stomach, elbows brushing the sides.
Elbows just behind the trunk, shoulder blades together, chest up; do not lean far back.
Breathe in and let the arms reach forward under control, the shoulder blades sliding forward and the chest leaning slightly.
Brief stretch at full reach, back long, then row again.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the trunk far back to move the weight
mistakes.fix: Keep the lean small (about 15 degrees forward to upright); lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the lower back at the reach
mistakes.fix: Lean from the hips with a long spine; reach only as far as you can keep it.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
mistakes.fix: Think of pulling the shoulder blades back and down.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the handle to the chest
mistakes.fix: Row to the stomach, just below the ribs, with the forearms level.

kinematics.norm: From slightly forward at the reach to upright at the finish, with a neutral spine; rows with a supported or upright trunk kept lumbar loads lower than a free bent-over row (Fenwick 2009)
From nearly straight to about 90-100 degrees (clinical opinion)
Upper arm from in front of the body to just behind the trunk (clinical opinion)
Forward (protracted) at the reach, drawn together (retracted) at the finish; retraction work drives the middle trapezius and rhomboids (Oyama 2010)
Neutral (palms facing) on a close-grip V-handle (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s pull and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Low Seated Row, video (movement reference)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move with the trunk still and the shoulders down.
At the end of the set, lean forward and let the handle back to the stack slowly; do not let go at the finish.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low-back discomfort: keep the trunk upright the whole time (no lean at the reach) and bend the knees more (clinical opinion).
Shoulder discomfort at the reach: shorten the reach so the shoulders do not round forward.
regressions: Band seated row anchored at the feet.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back toward the side of the trunk.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back toward the side of the trunk.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blade back toward the spine at the finish.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blade back toward the spine at the finish.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps pull the upper arm back.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps pull the upper arm back.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow as the handle comes in.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbow as the handle comes in.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the spine long and the trunk still against the cable.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the spine long and the trunk still against the cable.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk so the arms, not a rock of the body, move the load.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.

guides.label: Handle to the stomach, elbows close
